concept.name: Short-sale restriction
aliases: short sale price test circuit breaker
concept.definition: A rule limiting when or at what price short sales may be executed, the current U.S. form being Rule 201 of Regulation SHO: when a stock's price falls at least 10% from the prior day's close, trading centers must prevent the execution or display of short-sale orders at prices at or below the national best bid for the rest of that day and the following day.
concept.intuition: When a stock is already crashing, this rule makes short sellers wait their turn above the bid so they can't keep hammering the price down tick after tick.
concept.mechanics: Rule 201 aims to let long sellers sell first on declining days and to prevent short selling — including potentially abusive short selling — from accelerating a severe intraday decline. Exchanges and trading centers maintain policies to block covered short sales at impermissible prices once the circuit breaker triggers; orders properly marked 'short exempt' are excepted.
concept.formula: Trigger: current price <= 0.90 x prior day's closing price; once triggered, short-sale orders may not execute or be displayed at a price <= national best bid for the remainder of the day and the next trading day.
concept.failure_modes: Studies of price tests (including the repealed uptick rule) found limited effect on declines, and restrictions can impair liquidity and price discovery in the very stocks under stress; determined sellers can route around the intent via options or exempt market-making channels.
concept.misconceptions: Rule 201 does not ban short selling in a declining stock — short sales remain permitted at prices above the bid; nor does a triggered restriction mean the stock is being manipulated, since it triggers mechanically on a 10% move.
concept.example: XYZ closes at $50 on Monday and trades down to $44.80 intraday Tuesday, triggering Rule 201; for the rest of Tuesday and all of Wednesday, short sales can only execute above the national best bid.

citations.source: SEC Office of Investor Education and Assistance, Key Points About Regulation SHO
citations.section: Section III: Rule 201 — Short Sale Price Test Circuit Breaker
